title: One Bag
audience: People who left a small town for a big city, and those who are about to. My friends who made the same journey watch it first, on their phones.
intent: They should recognise their own first night, and feel that being lost at the start is normal and worth living through.

style.block: Hand-painted gouache illustration with soft visible brush strokes and warm paper grain. The painting fills the whole frame from edge to edge. Muted earth palette with amber and teal accents. Gentle rim light, simple shapes, picture-book composition with the subject in the centre of the frame. No writing or lettering anywhere in the picture: number plates, shop signs and screens are plain blank shapes.
style.negative: text, letters, signs with writing, watermark, logo, photorealistic, extra fingers

characters.label: The author in 2019
characters.description: A slim Ethiopian young man of about nineteen with dark brown skin and short black curly hair. He wears a charcoal grey jacket over a white shirt, olive green trousers rolled at the ankle, and dark blue moulded plastic sandals with a closed toe and a buckle strap on bare feet. He carries one olive green canvas backpack.
characters.reference_prompt: One single full-length figure on a plain warm background, seen from behind, standing in a neutral pose with his backpack on his shoulders, his feet and sandals in view. Only one figure in the picture.

characters.label: The friend who knew the city
characters.description: An Ethiopian young man of about the same age, a little taller, with dark brown skin and short black hair, always seen from behind, wearing a blue denim jacket and carrying nothing.
characters.reference_prompt: One single full-length figure on a plain warm background, seen from behind, standing in a neutral pose with empty hands. Only one figure in the picture.

characters.label: The author today
characters.description: The same man seven years later, in his mid twenties, with dark brown skin and short black curly hair, calm, wearing a plain shirt, always seen from behind.

music.caption: Solo krar, the Ethiopian six-string lyre, plucked slowly. A sparse pentatonic melody in the tizita mood. One instrument only, in a quiet room. No drums, no vocals.
music.chosen_reason: Second set, candidate 2. A listening model hears a plucked string instrument and bells, slow, with no busy moment, where candidate 1 brings in a flute and candidate 3 percussion. Chosen from those descriptions by the coding agent, on the author's instruction to decide. The author has not compared the six by ear yet.

cues.note: Krar alone, very quiet. Midday, the goodbye.
The melody opens up with the road and the mountains.
Night in the city: the melody thins out, a low drone enters.
The busiest moment, the brokers. Still quiet under the voice.
Back to the krar alone. The room.
The first melody returns and resolves. Fade under the end card.

lines: Images, voice and music were generated by AI models.
A true story by Bete Goshme

shots.title: Midday, Ankober
shots.reason: Where it starts: a small highland town at midday and one backpack. The goodbye is said in the voice, because the friend who came to say it is not shown.

keyframe.prompt: Midday in a small town in the Ethiopian highlands. An old boxy country bus is parked across the picture, seen from its side: a row of windows, an open door, bundles tied on its roof rack. In front of it, in the centre, one young man seen from behind stands facing the open door, his backpack on his shoulders. Low houses with rusty corrugated tin roofs and mud-plastered walls, tall thin eucalyptus trees, red-brown dusty ground, high bright sun, short shadows. Nobody else in the foreground.

motion.prompt: He shifts the backpack on his shoulders and steps toward the bus door. Fixed camera.

narration.am: መስከረም ሁለት ሺህ አሥራ ሁለት። እኩለ ቀን ላይ ከአንኮበር ተነሳሁ። አንድ የጀርባ ቦርሳ ብቻ ይዤ። አንድ ጓደኛዬ ሸኘኝ።
narration.en: Meskerem 2012 (late 2019). At midday I left Ankober. Just one backpack. A friend saw me off.

shots.title: The gravel road
shots.reason: The journey itself, and the scale of it: one small bus on a gravel road under forested mountains. He said the view was amazing, so the shot is wide. It lasts no longer than its generated clip can move.

keyframe.prompt: Extreme wide view from high above: a pale gravel road winds along steep green mountainsides in the Ethiopian highlands. One tiny country bus on the road trails a long plume of dust. Dense dark green juniper and eucalyptus forest on the slopes, layer after layer of mountains fading into blue haze, early afternoon light. No people.

motion.prompt: The small bus moves slowly along the road and its dust drifts away. Slow pan to the right.

narration.am: እስከ ደብረ ብርሃን ድረስ ፒስታ መንገድ። ከዚያ በኋላ አስፋልት።
narration.en: A gravel road as far as Debre Birhan. After that, asphalt.

shots.title: The window seat
shots.reason: The same journey from where he sat. Nobody travelled with him, so the shot is his alone: he at the window, his backpack on the seat beside him, and the mountains outside.

keyframe.prompt: Inside an old country bus, the view runs along its left wall: a row of large side windows and, under them, the worn backs of passenger seats one behind another, getting smaller toward the far end of the bus. In the nearest seat a young passenger sits by the window, seen from behind and a little to the side: the back of his head, his shoulders and his arm above the worn back of his seat. He is turned to the window beside him, so his face cannot be seen. His backpack rests on the empty seat beside him. Through the windows, steep forested mountain slopes of the Ethiopian highlands in afternoon light.

motion.prompt: Forest and mountain slopes slide slowly past the window. Slight shake of a moving bus.

narration.am: በመስኮት በኩል ተቀመጥኩ። ውጪው ደንና ተራራ ብቻ። እይታው አስደነቀኝ።
narration.en: I sat by the window. Outside, only forest and mountain. The view amazed me.

shots.title: Lamberet at night
shots.reason: The arrival, and the turn of the film: daylight and mountains give way to night, crowds, lit buildings and cars. He is alone in the frame, facing all of it. His friend is somewhere in that crowd, and the voice says so.

keyframe.prompt: A wide night view of a busy avenue on the edge of Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, painted from the roadside: dense traffic of cars and blue and white minibus taxis with white headlights and red tail lights, pavements packed with people as dark shapes, tall concrete buildings with hundreds of lit windows, street lamps. Small in the lower part of the frame, seen from behind, one young man with his backpack on his shoulders stands at the roadside and looks at it all.

motion.prompt: Traffic moves slowly along the avenue: cars and minibuses roll forward and their headlights pass. The young man stands still with his back to us. The camera does not move.

narration.am: ላምበረት የደረስኩት ከመሸ በኋላ ነው። ጓደኛዬ እዚያው ጠበቀኝ። ሰው፣ መብራት፣ መኪና፤ ሁሉም በአንድ ጊዜ።
narration.en: I reached Lamberet after dark. My friend was there, waiting for me. People, lights, cars, everything at once.

review.note: Rewritten on 25 Nov after the first three listeners: fewer uses of the word for "was", and a story that says something to its audience. Written by the coding agent, whom the author told to decide the wording. Not confirmed by the author yet.

shots.title: Autobus Tera, from far
shots.reason: Where the night is going: the big bus station, seen whole and from far, before we are in the middle of it. No words, only the place.

keyframe.prompt: The paint covers the whole frame and runs off all four edges, with no paper showing. Wide view from a little above of a large bus station yard in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, at night: long rows of parked long-distance buses, tall lamp posts with warm light, dust hanging in the air, many small dark figures of people moving between the buses, and the dark city with a few lit windows behind. Nobody in the foreground.

motion.prompt: People move between the buses and the dust drifts in the lamp light. Slow push in.

review.note: A new picture on 26 Nov: the first one, blurred city lights, said nothing. The author said on 25 Nov that he was not sure about the vehicle they took, so none is shown.

shots.title: Do you want a bed?
shots.reason: The heart of the story as he tells it: not fear but confusion. Brokers on every side offering a bed, and two friends who have to pick one.

keyframe.prompt: Night in the yard of a big crowded bus station in Addis Ababa. In the centre, seen from behind, two young men stand close together: the shorter one with a backpack, the other in a blue denim jacket with nothing on his back. Around them five men in a half circle lean in and gesture with open hands. The five are painted as dark silhouettes against the bright yard lamps, with no faces to be seen. Behind them rows of parked long-distance buses and dust hanging in the light.

motion.prompt: The men around them gesture and step closer. Slow push in.

narration.am: አውቶቡስ ተራ ስንደርስ ደላሎች ከበቡን። «አልጋ ትፈልጋላችሁ?» «አልጋ?» ከየአቅጣጫው። ግራ ገባን። በመጨረሻ አንዱን መረጥን።
narration.en: At Autobus Tera the brokers closed in on us. "Do you want a bed?" "A bed?" From every side. We were lost. In the end we picked one.

review.note: Rewritten on 25 Nov after the first three listeners: fewer uses of the word for "was", and a story that says something to its audience. Written by the coding agent, whom the author told to decide the wording. Not confirmed by the author yet.

shots.title: The room
shots.reason: Quiet after the noise, and exactly as he described it: one bed, not very good, not bad, clean. The backpack is the only thing of his in it.

keyframe.prompt: A small plain rented room at night in Addis Ababa: one narrow single bed with one pillow and a clean sheet, neatly made, bare painted walls, a single bulb, an olive green canvas backpack on the floor beside the bed, one small window. Modest and clean.

motion.prompt: Very slow push in toward the bed and the backpack.

narration.am: ክፍሉ ባለ አንድ አልጋ። በጣም ጥሩ አይደለም፤ መጥፎም አይደለም። ግን ንጹሕ።
narration.en: One bed in the room. Not very good, not bad. But clean.

shots.title: The queue
shots.reason: The morning after: the city is ordinary again, a long line of people waiting for a ticket. He is the last one in it, seen from behind.

keyframe.prompt: Early morning in the open yard of a bus station in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, soft gold light and long shadows. One single-file queue of men and women, all seen from behind and standing one behind another, runs in a long curve across the yard to a small ticket window in a low building. A young man with his backpack on his shoulders is the last person in the queue, nearest to us, seen from behind. Long-distance buses are parked along one side.

motion.prompt: The queue shuffles forward a step. Slow pan along the line.

narration.am: ጠዋት ረጅም ሰልፍ ተሰልፈን ትኬት ቆረጥን።
narration.en: In the morning we stood in a long queue and got the ticket.

review.note: Written by the coding agent on 25 Nov from the author's words that day: "in morning we got ticjet via long que". The film does not say where the ticket was for. Not confirmed by the author yet.

shots.title: Now
shots.reason: The answer to the whole night, in two words of his. The same city, seen calmly by the man that boy became, with the old backpack on the wall beside him.

keyframe.prompt: Golden hour. A wide view from the back of a balcony: its bare floor in the foreground, a low wall across the picture, and beyond the wall the wide city of Addis Ababa: low tin-roofed houses mixed with mid-rise concrete and glass buildings, eucalyptus-covered hills on the horizon and a wide sky. In the middle of the picture one man alone, seen from behind, stands at the wall. His whole figure from head to feet is small in the frame and takes half of the picture's height. An old, worn olive green canvas backpack stands on the floor against his leg. Nothing is on his back. Calm warm light.

motion.prompt: A light wind moves his shirt and the first city lights come on far away. He stands still. Slow pull out.

narration.am: ዛሬ ያንን የመጀመሪያ ሌሊት ሳስታውስ፣ ከቤቱ ለሚወጣ ሁሉ አንድ ነገር እላለሁ፦ የመጀመሪያው ሌሊት ሁሌም ግራ ያጋባል። አትሽሽ። አጣጥመው።
narration.en: Today, remembering that first night, I tell all who leave home one thing: the first night is always confusing. Do not run from it. Savour it.
